events.title: The trial of Joan of Arc begins
events.summary: The 19-year-old faces more than 70 accusations.
events.description: On January 9, 1431, Joan of Arc, then 19 years old, was put on trial in Rouen, France, facing more than 70 accusations. Two years earlier she had led the French to victory at Orleans.
events.notificationTitle: Joan of Arc goes on trial
events.notificationBody: In 1431, the trial of Joan of Arc began in Rouen.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 9
Encyclopaedia Britannica - Saint Joan of Arc

events.title: Simone de Beauvoir is born in Paris
events.summary: The writer and feminist thinker is born.
events.description: On January 9, 1908, Simone de Beauvoir, a writer and feminist who gave literary form to the themes of existentialism, was born in Paris.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 9

events.title: Mahmoud Abbas is elected Palestinian Authority president
events.summary: He succeeds Yasser Arafat as leader of the Palestinian Authority.
events.description: On January 9, 2005, Mahmoud Abbas was elected president of the Palestinian Authority.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 9

events.title: Apple introduces iTunes
events.summary: The digital media player changes how people buy and play music.
events.description: On January 9, 2001, Apple introduced iTunes, a digital media player application that went on to revolutionize digital music.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 9

events.title: Julius Caesar crosses the Rubicon
events.dateNote: Traditional date in the pre-Julian Roman calendar.
events.summary: Caesar leads his army into Italy, starting a civil war.
events.description: On January 10, 49 BCE, Julius Caesar and his army crossed the Rubicon to take control of the Roman Republic, a step that began a civil war.
events.notificationBody: In 49 BCE, Julius Caesar led his army across the Rubicon.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 10

events.title: Thomas Paine publishes Common Sense
events.summary: The pamphlet calls for American independence.
events.description: On January 10, 1776, Thomas Paine published Common Sense, a 50-page pamphlet that sold more than 500,000 copies within a few months and called for a war of independence.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 10

events.title: The League of Nations is established
events.summary: The first international peacekeeping organization comes into being.
events.description: On January 10, 1920, the League of Nations was established, with its headquarters in Geneva.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 10

events.title: The first UN General Assembly meets in London
events.summary: Delegates of the new United Nations gather for the first time.
events.description: On January 10, 1946, the first United Nations General Assembly met in London.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 10

events.title: Radar signals are bounced off the Moon
events.summary: Echoes from the Moon are detected for the first time.
events.description: On January 10, 1946, radar signals bouncing off the Moon were detected for the first time.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 10

events.title: Shelley's 'Ozymandias' is published
events.summary: The sonnet about a ruined statue appears in print for the first time.
events.description: On January 11, 1818, Percy Bysshe Shelley's sonnet 'Ozymandias' was published for the first time.
events.notificationTitle: Look on my works, ye Mighty
events.notificationBody: In 1818, Shelley's sonnet Ozymandias was first published.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 11

events.title: The US surgeon general links smoking to lung cancer
events.summary: A landmark report changes public views of cigarettes.
events.description: On January 11, 1964, US Surgeon General Luther L. Terry announced that cigarette smoking is linked to lung cancer.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 11

events.title: Amelia Earhart flies solo from Hawaii to California
events.dateNote: She left Honolulu on January 11 and landed in Oakland the next day.
events.summary: She completes the first successful solo flight of about 2,400 miles.
events.description: On January 11, 1935, Amelia Earhart set off on the first successful solo flight from Hawaii to California, a distance of about 2,400 miles.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 11
Encyclopaedia Britannica - Amelia Earhart

events.title: Sir Edmund Hillary dies
events.summary: The New Zealand mountaineer dies at 88.
events.description: On January 11, 2008, Sir Edmund Hillary, the New Zealand mountaineer, died at age 88.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 11

events.title: Jean Chretien is born
events.summary: The future prime minister of Canada is born.
events.description: On January 11, 1934, Jean Chretien was born. He served as prime minister of Canada from 1993 to 2003.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 11

events.title: Berry Gordy launches Tamla Records
events.summary: Gordy starts the Detroit record business that becomes Motown.
events.description: On January 12, 1959, Berry Gordy launched Tamla Records, a major step toward transforming American music.
events.notificationTitle: The start of the Motown sound
events.notificationBody: In 1959, Berry Gordy launched Tamla Records.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 12
Encyclopaedia Britannica - Motown

events.title: A magnitude-7.0 earthquake strikes Haiti
events.summary: The quake devastates Port-au-Prince and the surrounding region.
events.description: On January 12, 2010, a magnitude-7.0 earthquake devastated Haiti, killing more than 300,000 people.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 12

events.title: NASA launches Deep Impact
events.summary: The probe is sent to study comet Tempel 1.
events.description: On January 12, 2005, the US space probe Deep Impact was launched to study comet Tempel 1.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 12

events.title: Britain ends the state of emergency in Kenya
events.summary: The emergency declared during the Mau Mau Rebellion is lifted.
events.description: On January 12, 1960, the British government ended the state of emergency it had declared in Kenya during the Mau Mau Rebellion.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 12

events.title: Hattie Caraway is elected to the US Senate
events.summary: She becomes the first woman elected to the Senate.
events.description: On January 12, 1932, Hattie Ophelia Caraway became the first woman elected to the US Senate.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 12

events.title: Emile Zola publishes 'J'accuse'
events.summary: His open letter denounces the army over the Dreyfus affair.
events.description: On January 13, 1898, the novelist Emile Zola published an open letter titled 'J'accuse', denouncing the French general staff for its role in the 1894 treason court-martial of Alfred Dreyfus.
events.notificationBody: In 1898, Emile Zola published J'accuse over the Dreyfus affair.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 13

events.title: Johnny Cash records live at Folsom Prison
events.summary: He performs for about 2,000 inmates.
events.description: On January 13, 1968, Johnny Cash recorded the album Johnny Cash at Folsom Prison in front of an audience of some 2,000 inmates.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 13

events.title: Douglas Wilder is sworn in as governor of Virginia
events.summary: He is the first popularly elected African American governor in the US.
events.description: On January 13, 1990, Douglas Wilder was sworn in as governor of Virginia, the first popularly elected African American governor in the United States.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 13

events.title: The Costa Concordia runs aground off Italy
events.summary: The cruise ship capsizes off Giglio Island.
events.description: On January 13, 2012, the cruise ship Costa Concordia, carrying some 4,200 people, ran aground and capsized off Giglio Island in Italy. Thirty-two people died.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 13

events.title: The Huygens probe lands on Titan
events.summary: A spacecraft touches down on Saturn's largest moon.
events.description: On January 14, 2005, the Huygens probe landed on Titan, Saturn's largest moon, the first landing on a world in the outer solar system.
events.notificationBody: In 2005, the Huygens probe landed on Saturn's largest moon, Titan.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 14
NASA Science - Huygens probe

events.title: Puccini's Tosca premieres in Rome
events.summary: The opera opens at the Teatro Costanzi.
events.description: On January 14, 1900, Giacomo Puccini's opera Tosca had its world premiere at Rome's Costanzi Theatre.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 14

events.title: Tunisia's President Ben Ali steps down
events.summary: Mass protests force him from power.
events.description: On January 14, 2011, Tunisian President Zine al-Abidine Ben Ali stepped down following mass protests in what became known as the Jasmine Revolution.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 14

events.title: Congress ratifies the Treaty of Paris
events.summary: The peace formally ends the American Revolution.
events.description: On January 14, 1784, the Continental Congress ratified the Peace of Paris, formally ending the American Revolution.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 14

events.title: Queen Margrethe II of Denmark abdicates
events.summary: Frederik X becomes king after her 52-year reign.
events.description: On January 14, 2024, Queen Margrethe II of Denmark abdicated after 52 years on the throne, and Crown Prince Frederik became King Frederik X.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 14

events.title: The British Museum opens to the public
events.summary: London's museum welcomes visitors six years after its founding act.
events.description: On January 15, 1759, the British Museum opened to the public in London. It had been established by an act of Parliament in 1753.
events.notificationBody: In 1759, the British Museum opened its doors to the public.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 15

events.title: Wikipedia launches
events.summary: The free online encyclopedia goes live.
events.description: On January 15, 2001, Wikipedia, a free Internet-based encyclopedia with an open-source management style, debuted.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 15

events.title: The Great Molasses Flood hits Boston
events.summary: A tank collapse sends over two million gallons through the North End.
events.description: On January 15, 1919, a storage tank collapsed in Boston, sending more than two million gallons of molasses flowing through the city's North End.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 15

events.title: US Airways Flight 1549 lands on the Hudson River
events.summary: Captain Chesley Sullenberger brings the airliner down on the river.
events.description: On January 15, 2009, US Airways Flight 1549, piloted by Captain Chesley ('Sully') Sullenberger, landed in the Hudson River in New York.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 15

events.title: Rosa Luxemburg is murdered in Berlin
events.summary: The revolutionary is killed after the Spartacist uprising.
events.description: On January 15, 1919, the revolutionary Rosa Luxemburg was arrested and murdered in Berlin, accused of fomenting the uprising known as the Spartacus Revolt.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 15
